newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers as dlr gains capped, eyes on baht.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers as dlr gains capped, eyes on baht.

text.p: The ringgit recovered after dollar gains were again capped, but the trading range was kept tight as players directed their attention to the baht.
The baht fell sharply on Thursday after news that Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan had resigned.
Dealers said news that Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee also planned to tender his resignation would prompt further selling of baht.
"Players are mostly looking at the baht and not doing much on dollar/ringgit. The baht's fall today has little effect on ringgit," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.
Dealers said a continuation of Wednesday's short-covering pushed the dollar higher at the opening but its rise was capped by local exporters selling interest at 2.5170/80.
Buying orders out of Hong Kong at 2.5130 helped limit the dollar's downside, they said.

Dealers said the dollar might again test higher levels against the ringgit but Bank Negara's recent firm stance on speculative activities and fears of central bank intervention should cap its rise at 2.5200 for the time being.
Players sold dollar/ringgit on Wednesday amid talk that Bank Negara had warned local banks about lending money offshore to speculative funds.

The talk gave the ringgit some relief against the dollar as the Malaysian unit was seen to be on the defensive over lingering concerns about Malaysia's poor trade data -- a deficit of 2.1 billion ringgit for April after a 1.75 billion ringgit surplus in March.
At 0930 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5160/70 a dollar against 2.5142/52 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
Dealers said they expected dollar/ringgit to trade in a 2.4950-2.5200 range in the near-term.
